St. Louis Fed's Musalem says four more rate hikes may be needed in coming months
body: St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months, offering one of the most hawkish views yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation.
During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case that current policy is not significantly restricting economic activity.
"The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he said.

Musalem said the real policy rate, which subtracts the inflation rate from the Fed's target rate, needs to be between 2%-2.5% by next spring, and estimated that the current rate is about a full point below that range. That position suggests the Fed may need to hike at each of the upcoming Fed meetings in December, January, March and April.

Musalem does not get a vote on the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee over the period where he says that the rate increases will be needed, though he does get to present views and provide input on the "dot plot" of individual members' expectations. He will next vote in 2028.
To be sure, Musalem noted "an unlikely but still plausible scenario" in which no further hikes would be needed.

"Falling energy prices and lower shipping costs, or an increase in potential output growth driven by higher productivity growth, might ease inflation pressures such that inflation moves toward target in 18 months," he said. Another possibility is that demand might decelerate as spending on artificial intelligence slows.

However, he said the more likely scenario is that "persistent strong demand and ongoing supply pressures" combine to keep inflation above the Fed's 2% target, thus requiring further increases in the fed funds rate from its current range of 3.75%-4%.

"It would be preferable for a higher real policy rate to happen in a balanced way, driven both by lower inflation and a higher nominal policy rate," he said. "However, the nominal policy rate may need to do most of the work."

news.title: investingLive European news wrap: Risk sentiment remains tentative amid hawkish Fed and US-Iran stalemate
body: The main highlight in the session was the UK labour market report. The data was generally mixed, with the unemployment rate falling to 4.6% and employment rising by a stronger than expected 156K. However, the ONS expressed concerns about survey composition, while October payrolls showed a 34K decline and vacancies continued to fall. Wage growth also moderated, with regular earnings slowing to 3.5% y/y from 3.7%, although total pay growth including bonuses eased to 3.6%. Public sector pay remained significantly stronger than private sector pay, while real regular wage growth was modest at just 0.4%.

This data didn't change anything for the Bank of England's outlook, as the central bank will likely seek further evidence that wage inflation is easing sustainably before gaining confidence in the broader inflation outlook. Markets are still pricing in an 89% probability of a rate hike in December and a cumulative 95 bps of tightening by the end of 2027.

We also got the November German ZEW survey which showed a stronger than expected improvement in economic sentiment, with the Economic Sentiment Index rising to 35.6 from 28.1 and the Expectations Index climbing to 26.5 from 18.5, while current conditions improved slightly to -33.2 but remained firmly negative. The recovery is being supported by rising manufacturing orders and lower oil prices, although the outlook remains uneven across sectors.

Government spending remains a key driver of activity, but concerns are growing over the sustainability of rising public debt. Eurozone expectations also improved, rising 8 points to 26.5, while current conditions remained weak at -14.7. The survey points to improving confidence but doesn't change the ECB outlook, with a December rate hike fully priced in and markets expecting at least one further increase next year.Lasty, Fed's Musalem delivered his usual hawkish remarks, warning of a meaningful risk that inflation will remain elevated unless the Fed acts soon, saying that several rate hikes are likely needed before spring. He argued that moving early is the best way to bring price pressures under control without damaging jobs and economic growth, while stressing that the Fed's resolve is important to maintaining confidence, as doubts could push bond yields higher. Despite the inflation concerns, Musalem remains optimistic that above-trend GDP growth can continue, noting that monetary policy and financial conditions are still providing tailwinds.

news.title: Solana's recovery hinges on the Fed and US-Iran breakthrough as risk sentiment remains negative
body: Solana has been under heavy selling pressure over the past week as the risk sentiment in the crypto market deteriorated amid the hawkish Fed repricing and US-Iran tensions.

The main catalyst was Fed's Waller speech, in which he opened the door for a larger 50 bps hike at the December meeting. His remarks triggered a strong hawkish repricing, which was then exacerbated by the hotter than expected US CPI data.
Then, we got Trump saying on Truth Social that the US doesn't need a deal with Iran, adding to inflation and growth concerns and putting further pressure on risk assets.

Looking ahead, the bearish trend will likely persist amid the hawkish Fed and prolonged US-Iran standoff. A more dovish Fed or a breakthrough in the US-Iran situation will likely be needed to trigger a sustained recovery and reverse the current trend.

On the daily chart, we can see that Solana extended the selloff in the past week amid the hawkish repricing and the increased US-Iran tensions. If we get a pullback, we can expect the sellers to lean on the major downward trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the 125.00 level next.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a minor downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. The sellers will likely lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break higher to pile in for a rally into new highs, with the major downward trendline as the first target.

On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor upward trendline defining the current pullback. We can expect the buyers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk below it, to keep targeting new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break lower to increase the bearish bets into the 60.00 level next. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

Today we get the US Retail Sales. Tomorrow, we have the FOMC meeting minutes. On Thursday, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. The focus will remain on Fed speakers and the US-Iran developments.

news.title: Crude oil erases recent gains despite no change in the US-Iran situation. What's next?
body: Crude oil erased all the recent gains yesterday despite no change in the US-Iran situation. There is a scenario where oil prices could fall without a change in the US-Iran situation, but we would need strong growth fears to make the market to shift the focus to demand destruction.

On the news side, US Vice President Vance said that the campaign against Iran will not become an endless war and expressed confidence in Trump's ability to bring it to an end. Meanwhile, Secretary of State Rubio reaffirmed Washington's security commitment to Bahrain following Iranian attacks.

Iran continues to take a hardline stance on the Strait of Hormuz, insisting that it remains under full Iranian control and will stay closed unless the US accepts its conditions. Saudi Arabia was also reportedly involved in a new attack.

Overall,the situation remains unchanged, with diplomatic efforts continuing without any meaningful breakthrough yet. It goes without saying that a breakthrough would trigger a significant selloff and take oil prices back to pre-war levels relatively quickly. But as of now, this scenario doesn’t look likely.

An escalation or a prolonged stalemate should keep oil prices supported, although there’s also a chance that Trump decides to proceed with limited strikes against Iran’s nuclear facilities before exiting the war.

On the daily chart, we can see that crude oil (CFD contract) continues to consolidate around the key 87.00 handle amid the prolonged US-Iran stalemate. We can expect the sellers to continue to pile in below the 87.00 handle to keep targeting the 80.00 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price rising back above the 87.00 handle, to position for a rally into the 110.00 resistance next.

On the 4 hour chart, we can see the price broke below the minor upward trendline that was defining the near-term recovery. If we get a retest of the broken trendline, we can expect the sellers to step in, with a defined risk above the trendline, to position for a drop into the 80.00 handle. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price rising back above the trendline to position for a rally into the 110.00 resistance, with the 92.50 level as the first target.

On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here as the sellers will have a better risk to reward setup around the broken trendline, while the buyers will need to see the price rising back above it to start positioning for new highs. The red lines define the average daily range for today.
Today we get the US Retail Sales. Tomorrow, we have the FOMC meeting minutes. On Thursday, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. The focus will remain on US-Iran developments.

news.title: Ethereum's bearish trend could extend further without a dovish Fed pivot or a US-Iran breakthrough
body: Ethereum has faced significant selling pressure over the past week, with a big wave of liquidations across the crypto market as the hawkish Fed repricing tightened financial conditions and weighed on risk sentiment.

The main catalyst was Fed's Waller speech, in which he also floated the possibility of a larger 50 bps hike at the December meeting. His remarks triggered a strong hawkish repricing, which was then exacerbated by the higher than expected US CPI data.
The risk sentiment deteriorated further when Trump said on Truth Social that the US doesn't need a deal with Iran, adding to inflation and growth concerns.

Looking ahead, Ethereum will likely remain under pressure as long as the negative macro backdrop persists. A more dovish Fed or a breakthrough in the US-Iran situation will likely be needed to trigger a reversal in the bearish trend.

On the daily chart, we can see that Ethereum extended the losses as the risk sentiment deteriorated last week. The price is now consolidating below the 1,870 level. The sellers will likely continue to step in around these levels, with a defined risk above the 1,870 level, to keep targeting the 1,500 level next. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price rising back above the 1,870 level to start positioning for a correction into the major downward trendline.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. We can expect the sellers to continue to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting the 1,500 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a correction into the major downward trendline.

The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break lower to increase the bearish bets into the 1,500 level next. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

news.title: Gold consolidates as growth concerns gain traction amid a falling stock market. What's next?
body: Gold is now consolidating below key resistance levels, having so far resisted pressure from another rise in real yields and the US dollar. This might be an early signal of a change in momentum, although a technical breakout might still be needed given the current headwinds.

The hawkish repricing should now be mostly over, as a rate hike in December is widely expected, while the probability of a 50 bps hike remains very slim given that the majority of Fed members favour smaller steps.

It looks like growth concerns are finally gaining traction, with the stock market erasing almost all of last week's gains and Treasury yields slowly rolling over. These concerns are likely to persist and might even intensify as long as the US-Iran situation remains unresolved, and the Fed maintains the hawkish stance.

I think that in the current context, a prolonged US-Iran stalemate or an escalation would keep inflation expectations high alongside a weakening growth outlook, creating a stagflationary environment. And this should ultimately be bullish for gold.
At the same time, if there’s a breakthrough, we could see a dovish repricing on easing inflation concerns, which should also support gold in the short-term.

There are certainly strong headwinds for gold at the moment amid rising real yields and stronger US dollar, so these fundamental views will need to be paired with technicals for a confirmation of a change in momentum.

On the daily chart, we can see that gold (CFD contract) is consolidating below the key resistance zone around the 3,885 level and the major upward trendline. We can expect the sellers to continue to step in around these levels, with a defined risk above the broken trendline, to extend the drop into the 3,500 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price rising back above the broken trendline to start piling in for a rally into the 4,700 level next.

On the 4 hour chart, we can see the price broke above the downward trendline that was defining the bearish momentum. This might be an early signal of a change in momentum. The buyers will want to see the price rising back above the broken trendline to confirm the potential reversal and pile in for a rally into the 4,700 level, with the 4,150 level as the first target. The sellers, on the other hand, will continue to step in around these levels to keep targeting new lows.

On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here given the consolidation. The sellers will continue to step in around these levels to keep targeting new lows, while the buyers will need to see the price rising back above the broken trendline to start positioning for new highs. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

Today we get the US Retail Sales. Tomorrow, we have the FOMC meeting minutes. On Thursday, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. The focus will remain on Fed speakers and the US-Iran developments.
